g.text: Visual comparison of how each heuristic measures distance across a 2D discrete grid from Start (2, 8) to Goal (10, 2)
Why Does the Angle Matter for Pathfinding?
• Euclidean assumes the robot can drive along angle θ = 36.87° continuously.
• Manhattan cannot cut across angle θ; it projects θ onto orthogonal 0° & 90° axes.
• Chebyshev cuts diagonally at 45° for 6 steps, then straight at 0° for 2 steps.
• Dijkstra has NO angle (θ is undefined/omnidirectional), wasting work in all directions.
• Straight line cuts across grid tiles.
h = 0 ⟹ Priority f = g (Cost so far)
• Spreads like circular ripple in water.
h_Dijkstra (0) < h_Chebyshev (8) < h_Euclidean (10) < h_Manhattan (14) = h* (14 Optimal Steps)
